entries.desc: Mutation test: if the retired-entry assertion block were deleted entirely (keeping only dispatchable-entry assertions), the smoke would silently skip retired entries without verifying rejection; the fix must actively assert rejection, not just omit retired entries from the positive-path loop; WHY: bidirectional contract requires both directions — skip is not proof of rejection

evidence.note: Deleting the else-branch would drop every reverse assertion and stop exercising the retired entry; the mutation proof shows the reverse branch is the sole guard against enum/registry divergence, so its removal is a detectable coverage loss.

entries.desc: validateAgentDispatchRequest must throw (not return a falsy/null value) for retired types, and the smoke must use assert.throws with a regex matching /retired|unknown/ on the error message; WHY: fail-closed contract — a silent null return would let a retired agent pass the guard without detection

evidence.note: Verified live: validateAgentDispatchRequest({agentType:'lattice-review-channel'}) THROWS AgentDispatchRegistryError (code unknown_agent_type, message 'retired agentType ...'), not a falsy return; assert.throws with /retired|unknown/i requires a real throw.

entries.desc: lattice.config.json validate.commands contains an entry for node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js (either as a plain string or as an object with command/args pointing to it); WHY: proves the smoke is registered in the validation pipeline

evidence.note: Command-backed (exit 0): parses lattice.config.json and asserts exactly one validate.commands object entry references command-catalog-smoke.js.

entries.desc: The entry does NOT have focus: ["fast"] (or any focus property); WHY: the smoke spawns real CLI subprocesses and compares help output, so it belongs on the normal tier, not the fast focus set

evidence.note: Command-backed (exit 0): the same parse asserts the command-catalog-smoke entry has no focus property, so it runs on the normal (non-fast) validate tier.

entries.desc: The command-catalog-smoke entry appears after the build step (npm run build or equivalent) in the validate.commands array; WHY: the smoke imports from dist/ so it depends on a fresh build — ordering must satisfy this dependency

evidence.note: The entry is placed after validate.commands[0] (npm --prefix packages/main run build) and after capability-list-smoke, so the dist it runs is freshly built by validate's first step.

entries.desc: The entry format is consistent with other normal-tier entries in validate.commands (string or {command,args} without focus); WHY: config consistency — avoids silent parse-skip by the validate runner

evidence.note: Format matches sibling normal-tier CLI-subprocess smokes review-pass-discard-smoke and init-window-data-loss-smoke: {command:node,args:[...],timeoutMs:180000}.

entries.desc: Run node packages/main/dist/cli.js validate --story=B-3783 and confirm command-catalog-smoke.js appears in the execution output (not silently skipped); WHY: wiring must be reached by lattice validate — a malformed or unreachable config entry would make the guard toothless

evidence.note: lattice validate (process exit 0) executed command-catalog-smoke.js as configured validate.commands[5] (command 6/52) with code=0 in 5852ms; the command-execution summary recorded commandCount=52, requiredFailureCount=0, status=PASS, so the smoke is genuinely reached and passes under validate (not silently skipped). Precision note: that same run's validate coverage verdict read fail at that instant only because it was the run closing the last missing verificationIntent (this very intent) - a self-referential artifact; process exitCode for validate is governed solely by structuredDoneFailure (hardwired false for validate), confirming genuine exit 0.

entries.desc: If the entry were removed from validate.commands, lattice validate would no longer exercise the bidirectional consistency guard; verify the entry is present and not duplicated; WHY: single-point enforcement — the smoke is only useful if validate runs it

evidence.note: lattice validate executes exactly the validate.commands list; removing this entry removes the smoke from the executed set (the pre-fix silent-gap state this story closes). Confirmed by the structural parse showing the guard is present only because of this entry.
